subject: math
title: Grade 4 Decimal Tenths
seo_title: Grade 4 Decimal Tenths Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Read, represent, compare, and order decimal tenths, in various contexts
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on decimal tenths for the Ontario curriculum: tenths on strips and number lines, decimals greater than 1, comparing and ordering, fractions like 1/2 = 0.5, and adding and subtracting tenths. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Tenths are the first place after the decimal point: 3/10 = 0.3, and 10 tenths make 1 whole.
body_html:
Tenths

Split 1 whole into 10 equal parts. Each part is one tenth: 110 = 0.1. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point.

On a number line from 0 to 1 with 10 equal spaces, each space is 0.1.

Decimals greater than 1

Ten tenths make 1 whole. Write the wholes before the decimal point and the tenths after it.

Fractions and decimals

A fraction in tenths is easy to write as a decimal: 710 = 0.7. Halves and fifths can be changed to tenths first.

FractionTenthsDecimal
125100.5
152100.2
254100.4
Example 1

Write 3 510 as a decimal.

3 wholes go before the point. 5 tenths go in the first place after it.

Answer: 3.5

Comparing decimals

Compare the ones first. If the ones are the same, compare the tenths.

Example 2

Order 1.2, 0.9 and 2.1 from smallest to greatest.

Compare the ones: 0, 1 and 2.

Answer: 0.9, 1.2, 2.1

Adding and subtracting tenths

Add or take away the tenths, and remember that 10 tenths make 1 whole. Making the next whole number helps.

Example 3

0.6 + 0.7 = ?

0.6 + 0.4 = 1. Then add the other 0.3.

Answer: 1.3

Example 4

3.2 − 0.5 = ?

3.2 − 0.2 = 3. Then take away the other 0.3.

Answer: 2.7

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
0.5 = 150.5 = 510 = 12, and 15 = 0.2
0.10 > 0.9 because 10 > 90.10 = 0.1, and 1 tenth < 9 tenths
Writing 310 as 3.10 or 0.03Tenths use the first place: 0.3
0.6 + 0.7 = 0.1313 tenths = 1 whole and 3 tenths: 1.3
Counting 0.8, 0.9, 0.1010 tenths make 1 whole: 0.8, 0.9, 1

faq.q: What do Grade 4 students learn about decimals in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario math curriculum, Grade 4 students read, show, compare and order decimal tenths, connect them to fractions like 3/10 = 0.3 and 1/2 = 0.5, and add and subtract tenths in their heads. Hundredths come in Grade 5.

faq.q: How do you explain decimal tenths to a child?
faq.a: Show a strip or a chocolate bar split into 10 equal parts. Each part is one tenth, 0.1, so 3 parts are 0.3 and 10 parts make 1 whole.
No. 0.5 means 5 tenths, which is 5/10 or one half. One fifth is 2/10, so 1/5 = 0.2.
No. 0.10 is the same as 0.1, just 1 tenth, while 0.9 is 9 tenths. Compare the tenths digits, not the number of digits.

sets.title: Tenths with strips and number lines

items.q: The strip is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The strip is 1 whole split into 10 equal parts, so each part is 1 tenth. 3 parts are shaded: 310 = 0.3. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point. 3.10 mixes up the fraction and the decimal: it means 3 wholes and more.

items.q: The strip is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The strip is 1 whole split into 10 equal parts, so each part is 1 tenth. 7 parts are shaded: 710 = 0.7. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point. 0.3 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: The strip is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The strip is 1 whole split into 10 equal parts, so each part is 1 tenth. 5 parts are shaded: 510 = 0.5. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point. 5 would mean 5 whole strips.

items.q: 1 whole is split into 10 equal parts. What decimal is each part?
items.e: Each part is 110 of the whole, one tenth: 0.1. 1.10 is a mistake from writing the 1 and the 10 of 110 with a point between them.

items.q: How many tenths make 1 whole?
items.e: 1 whole split into 10 equal parts: 1010 = 1. So 10 tenths make 1 whole.

items.q: Which decimal is 4 tenths?
items.e: 4 tenths = 410. Write 0, the decimal point, then 4 in the tenths place: 0.4. 4 would be 4 wholes.

items.q: All four strips are the same size. Which strip shows 0.6?
items.e: 0.6 is 6 tenths, so the strip must have 10 equal parts with 6 shaded: strip B. A shows 0.4. C shows 16. D has 6 shaded, but it has 12 parts, so it shows one half.

items.q: The strip is 1 whole. What decimal is not shaded?
items.e: 6 of the 10 parts are shaded, so 10 − 6 = 4 parts are not shaded: 410 = 0.4. 0.6 is the shaded part.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 has 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 tenth (0.1). The dot is 3 spaces after 0: 0.3.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: Each of the 10 spaces is 0.1. The dot is 8 spaces after 0: 0.8. (0.2 counts the 2 spaces back from 1, the wrong end.)

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: Each space is 0.1. The dot is 2 spaces after 0.5: 0.5, 0.6, 0.7. 0.2 counts only the spaces after 0.5.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: The dot is 1 space after 0. Each space is 1 tenth: 0.1. 1 is the end of the line.

items.q: The red dot is halfway between 0 and 1. What decimal is it at?
items.e: The dot is 5 spaces after 0, and each space is 0.1: 0.5. 0.2 comes from the 2 in one half (12), but one half is 5 tenths.

items.q: Which point is at 0.4?
items.e: Each space is 0.1. Count 4 spaces from 0: point B. A is 0.2, C is 0.6 and D is 0.9.

items.q: Which point is at 0.8?
items.e: Each space is 0.1. Count 8 spaces from 0 (or 2 back from 1): point D. A is 0.1, B is 0.3 and C is 0.5.

items.q:
Count on in tenths. What comes next?
0.4, 0.5, 0.6, ?
items.e: Each step adds 1 tenth: 6 tenths + 1 tenth = 7 tenths = 0.7. 0.8 skips a number.

items.q:
Count on in tenths. What comes next?
0.7, 0.8, 0.9, ?
items.e: 9 tenths and 1 more make 10 tenths, which is 1 whole (1.0). 0.10 is not next: 0.10 is the same as 0.1, which is far back near 0.

items.q:
Count back in tenths. What comes next?
1, 0.9, 0.8, ?
items.e: Each step takes away 1 tenth: 8 tenths − 1 tenth = 7 tenths = 0.7. 1.1 counts up, and 0.6 skips a number.

items.q: Kai’s granola bar has 10 equal pieces. He eats 7 pieces. What decimal of the bar is left?
items.e: 10 − 7 = 3 pieces are left. Each piece is 1 tenth, so 310 of the bar is left: 0.3. 0.7 is the part he ate.

items.q: A garden has 10 equal rows. Maya plants carrots in 2 rows and beans in 5 rows. What decimal of the garden is planted?
items.e: 2 + 5 = 7 of the 10 rows are planted: 710 = 0.7. 0.3 is the part with no plants.

items.q: Each strip is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each strip is 1 whole. 1 whole strip is shaded (1) and 2 tenths of the last strip: 1 and 210 = 1.2. 0.12 would be less than 1.

items.q: Each strip is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each strip is 1 whole. 2 whole strips are shaded (2) and 3 tenths of the last strip: 2 and 310 = 2.3. 0.23 would be less than 1.

items.q: Each strip is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each strip is 1 whole. 3 whole strips are shaded (3) and 1 tenth of the last strip: 3 and 110 = 3.1. 0.31 would be less than 1.

items.q: Write 2 710 as a decimal.
items.e: 2 wholes, then the decimal point, then 7 tenths in the first place after the point: 2.7. 2.07 puts the 7 one place too far to the right.

items.q: Write 5 310 as a decimal.
items.e: The whole number goes before the point and the tenths after it: 5.3. 3.5 swaps them.

items.q: Which decimal is 4 ones and 6 tenths?
items.e: Ones go before the decimal point and tenths go right after it: 4.6.

items.q: How many tenths are there in 3.2?
items.e: 1 whole = 10 tenths, so 3 wholes = 30 tenths. 30 + 2 = 32 tenths. (2 is only the digit in the tenths place.)

items.q: How many tenths are there in 1.5?
items.e: 1 whole = 10 tenths. 10 + 5 = 15 tenths. (5 is only the digit in the tenths place.)

items.q: 26 tenths is the same as which decimal?
items.e: 10 tenths make 1 whole, so 20 tenths make 2 wholes. 26 tenths = 2 wholes and 6 tenths = 2.6.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 7.3?
items.e: The red 3 is in the first place after the decimal point, the tenths column. Its value is 3 tenths = 0.3.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 25.8?
items.e: The red 5 is just before the decimal point, in the ones column. Its value is 5 ones = 5.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 6 in 46.9?
items.e: In 46.9 the 6 is just before the decimal point, in the ones place. It is worth 6.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 13.4?
items.e: In 13.4 the 4 is right after the decimal point, in the tenths place. It is worth 4 tenths = 0.4.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: The line goes from 2 to 3 with 10 equal spaces, so each space is 0.1. The dot is 6 spaces after 2: 2.6. (2.4 counts back from 3, the wrong end.)

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: Between 4 and 5 there are 10 spaces, so each space is 0.1. The dot is 3 spaces after 5: 5.3. 5.7 counts back from 6.

items.q: Which point is at 2.4?
items.e: 2.4 is 4 tenths after 2. Count 4 spaces to the right of 2: point C. A is 1.4 (4 tenths after 1), B is 1.6 and D is 2.8.

items.q:
Count on in tenths. What comes next?
1.7, 1.8, 1.9, ?
items.e: 1.9 + 0.1: 9 tenths and 1 more make 10 tenths, which is 1 more whole. So 1 whole becomes 2: the next number is 2 (or 2.0). 1.10 is the same as 1.1.

items.q:
Count back in tenths. What comes next?
3.2, 3.1, 3, ?
items.e: 3 is the same as 30 tenths. 1 tenth less is 29 tenths: 2 wholes and 9 tenths = 2.9. 3.9 is much bigger than 3.

items.q: Owen’s ribbon is 2 m and 5 tenths of a metre long. How long is it as a decimal?
items.e: 2 whole metres and 510 of a metre: 2.5 m.

items.q: Each pizza at the class party is cut into 10 equal slices. There are 3 whole pizzas and 7 slices left. What decimal shows the pizza left?
items.e: 3 whole pizzas and 7 tenths of a pizza: 3 710 = 3.7 pizzas. 7.3 swaps the wholes and the tenths.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Both have 0 ones. Compare the tenths: 3 tenths < 7 tenths. So 0.3 < 0.7.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Both have 6 ones. Compare the tenths: 5 tenths < 7 tenths. So 6.5 < 6.7.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Compare the ones first: 1.4 has 1 one and 0.9 has 0 ones. So 1.4 > 0.9, even though 9 > 4.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Compare the ones first: 4 > 3. So 4.1 > 3.9. The tenths only matter when the ones are the same.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: 0.10 is the same as 0.1 (a 0 at the end does not change the value). 9 tenths > 1 tenth, so 0.9 > 0.10. Do not compare 9 with 10.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: 12.3 has 12 wholes and 9.8 has only 9 wholes. So 12.3 > 9.8.

items.q: Which number is greater than 2.5?
items.e: 3.1 has 3 ones, more than the 2 ones in 2.5. So 3.1 > 2.5. 1.9 is smaller even though 9 > 5: it has only 1 one.

items.q: Which number is between 1.4 and 1.8?
items.e: Count on in tenths from 1.4: 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, then 1.8. 1.3 is less than 1.4 and 1.9 is more than 1.8.

items.q: Which number is closest to 1?
items.e: 0.9 is just 1 tenth less than 1. 0.5 is 5 tenths away, and 0.1 and 1.9 are 9 tenths away. So 0.9 is the closest.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 0.8, 0.3, 0.5
items.e: All have 0 ones. Compare the tenths: 3, 5 and 8. Order: 0.3, 0.5, 0.8.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 1.2, 0.9, 2.1
items.e: Compare the ones first: 0.9 has 0, 1.2 has 1 and 2.1 has 2. Order: 0.9, 1.2, 2.1. 0.9 is not the biggest just because 9 is a big digit.

items.q: Which decimal is the greatest?
items.e: 0.9 and 0.10 have 0 ones. 1.1 and 1.2 both have 1 one; compare the tenths: 2 > 1. So 1.2 is the greatest. (0.10 = 0.1.)

items.q: Which decimal is the smallest?
items.e: 2.7 and 2.9 have the fewest ones (2). Compare their tenths: 7 < 9. So 2.7 is the smallest.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 4.2 and 4.7 both have 4 ones, and 2 tenths < 7 tenths. So 4.2 < 4.7 is true. 0.9 < 0.10 is false because 0.10 = 0.1.

items.q: Which point is at 1.3?
items.e: 1.3 is 3 tenths after 1. Count 3 spaces to the right of 1: point C. A is 0.3, B is 0.8 and D is 1.7.

items.q: Order from greatest to smallest: 3.4, 4.3, 3.9
items.e: 4.3 has the most ones, so it is the greatest. 3.9 > 3.4 (9 tenths > 4 tenths). Order: 4.3, 3.9, 3.4. Careful: the question asks for greatest first.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 0.9, 0.10, 0.5
items.e: 0.10 is the same as 0.1, just 1 tenth. Compare the tenths: 1, 5 and 9. Order: 0.10, 0.5, 0.9. 0.10 is not the biggest just because 10 is a bigger number than 9.

items.q: In the 60 m dash on track and field day, Chloe runs it in 9.8 seconds and Arjun runs it in 10.2 seconds. Who is faster?
items.e: In a race, the shorter time is faster. 9.8 has 9 wholes and 10.2 has 10 wholes, so 9.8 < 10.2. Chloe is faster.

items.q: Three bean plants in Ms. Patel’s class are 4.5 cm, 5.4 cm and 4.9 cm tall. How tall is the tallest plant?
items.e: 5.4 has 5 whole centimetres; the others have only 4. So 5.4 cm is the tallest, even though 4.9 has a 9.

items.q: In the long jump, Liam jumps 2.7 m, Noah jumps 2.9 m and Kai jumps 2.3 m. Who jumps the farthest?
items.e: All three jumps are 2 whole metres. Compare the tenths: 9 > 7 > 3. So Noah jumps the farthest.

items.q: Write 310 as a decimal.
items.e: 310 is 3 tenths. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point: 0.3. 3.10 just writes the 3 and the 10 with a point between them.

items.q: Write 910 as a decimal.
items.e: 910 is 9 tenths. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point: 0.9. 0.09 puts the 9 one place too far to the right.

items.q: Write 610 as a decimal.
items.e: 610 is 6 tenths. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point: 0.6. 0.4 is the part that is left (4 tenths).

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.3?
items.e: 0.3 has one digit after the point, so it means tenths: 3 tenths = 310. It is not 13: that would be 1 out of 3 equal parts.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.8?
items.e: One digit after the point means tenths: 0.8 = 8 tenths = 810. 210 is 0.2, the part that is left.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.5?
items.e: 0.5 = 5 tenths = 510 (which is also 12). It is not 15: one fifth is only 0.2.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 12?
items.e: Cut a whole into 10 equal parts: half of them is 5 parts. 12 = 510 = 0.5. 1.2 and 0.12 just copy the digits 1 and 2.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 15?
items.e: Cut a whole into 10 equal parts. 1 fifth of them is 2 parts: 15 = 210 = 0.2. 0.5 is a common mistake: 0.5 is one half, not one fifth.

items.q: Which one is not equal to 0.5?
items.e: 0.5 = five tenths = 510 = 12. But 15 = 210 = 0.2, so 15 is not equal to 0.5.

items.q: The two strips are the same size. What decimal of the top strip is shaded?
items.e: The top strip is in 5 equal parts, so each part is 15. Each fifth covers 2 tenths of the bottom strip. 2 fifths = 4 tenths: 25 = 410 = 0.4. 0.2 counts the parts but forgets they are fifths.

items.q: Which mixed number is equal to 1.7?
items.e: 1.7 = 1 whole and 7 tenths = 1 710. 710 forgets the whole.

items.q: Which mixed number is equal to 3.5?
items.e: 3.5 = 3 wholes and 5 tenths = 3 510. 3 15 is wrong: 0.5 is 510, not 15.

items.q: Write 1310 as a decimal.
items.e: 10 tenths make 1 whole, so 13 tenths = 1 whole and 3 tenths = 1.3.

items.q: How many tenths are equal to 12?
items.e: Half of 10 tenths is 5 tenths: 12 = 510 = 0.5.

items.q: Which fraction names the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 has 10 equal spaces, so each space is 110. The dot is 7 spaces after 0: 710 = 0.7. 310 counts back from 1.

items.q: Which is greater: 0.4 or 12?
items.e: 12 = 510 = 0.5, and 0.5 > 0.4. So 12 is greater.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 0.6, 12, 310
c: 0.6, 12, 310
12, 0.6, 310
12, 310, 0.6
310, 12, 0.6
items.e: Change them all to tenths: 310 = 0.3, 12 = 0.5 and 0.6. Order: 310, 12, 0.6.

items.q: Which pair shows two equal numbers?
items.e: 0.7 = 7 tenths = 710, so 0.7 and 710 are equal. 12 = 0.5 (not 0.2) and 15 = 0.2 (not 0.5).

items.q: Mei walks 12 km to school. Ethan walks 0.4 km. Who walks farther?
items.e: 12 km = 510 km = 0.5 km, and 0.5 > 0.4. So Mei walks farther.

items.q: A pan of brownies is cut into 10 equal pieces. The class eats 6 pieces. Which shows the part they eat?
items.e: 6 of the 10 equal pieces: 610 = 0.6. 410 and 0.4 is the part that is left.
4 tenths + 3 tenths = 7 tenths = 0.7. The answer is still in tenths, so it is not 0.07.
8 tenths + 2 tenths = 10 tenths, and 10 tenths make 1 whole: 1. 0.10 is only 1 tenth.
Make 1: 0.6 + 0.4 = 1, then add the other 0.3: 1.3. 13 tenths is 1 whole and 3 tenths, not 0.13.
1 = 10 tenths. 10 tenths − 4 tenths = 6 tenths = 0.6. 0.3 comes from 4 − 1, which is the wrong way round.
Add the ones: 2 + 1 = 3. Add the tenths: 5 + 3 = 8 tenths. So 2.5 + 1.3 = 3.8.
Make the next whole: 3.6 + 0.4 = 4, then add the other 0.4: 4.4. 3.14 writes 14 tenths in the tenths place; 14 tenths = 1 whole and 4 tenths.
Take away the ones: 4 − 1 = 3. Take away the tenths: 7 − 2 = 5. So 4.7 − 1.2 = 3.5. 5.9 adds instead.
Take away 0.2 to get to 3, then take away 0.3 more: 2.7. 3.3 does 5 − 2 because 2 − 5 looks hard; 3.7 adds instead of taking away.
Count up from 1.6: 0.4 makes 2, and 3 more makes 5. 0.4 + 3 = 3.4. 4.6 only takes away the 1 and forgets the 0.6.
Count up from 1.5 to 2: 5 tenths make the next whole. So the missing number is 0.5. 3.5 adds 1.5 + 2.

items.q: In the 60 m dash, Liam runs it in 10.4 seconds and Priya runs it in 9.8 seconds. How many seconds faster is Priya?
items.e: Count up from 9.8: 0.2 makes 10, then 0.4 more makes 10.4. 0.2 + 0.4 = 0.6 seconds. 1.4 takes 4 from 8 instead of 8 from 4.

items.q: Amira’s bean plant is 4.6 cm tall. It grows 1.5 cm in a week. How tall is it now?
items.e: 4.6 + 1 = 5.6, then 5.6 + 0.5: 0.4 makes 6 and 0.1 more makes 6.1 cm. 5.11 writes 11 tenths in the tenths place; 11 tenths = 1 whole and 1 tenth.

items.q: Lucas has 3 m of rope for a canoe trip. He cuts off 1.4 m. How much rope is left?
items.e: Count up from 1.4: 0.6 makes 2, and 1 more makes 3. 0.6 + 1 = 1.6 m. 2.6 only takes away the 1 whole; 4.4 adds.

items.q: Hana swims 25 m in 21.5 seconds. On her next try she is 0.7 seconds faster. What is her new time?
items.e: Faster means a shorter time, so subtract. 21.5 − 0.5 = 21, then take away 0.2 more: 20.8 seconds. 22.2 adds; 21.2 does 7 − 5.

items.q: On a snow day, 2.5 cm of snow falls in the morning and 3.8 cm falls in the afternoon. How much snow falls in all?
items.e: Ones: 2 + 3 = 5. Tenths: 5 + 8 = 13 tenths = 1 whole and 3 tenths. 5 + 1.3 = 6.3 cm. 1.3 is the difference, not the total.

items.q: At the Terry Fox Run, Ava walks 2.5 km and then runs 1.5 km. How far does she go in all?
items.e: Tenths: 5 + 5 = 10 tenths = 1 whole. Ones: 2 + 1 = 3, and 3 + 1 = 4 km. 3.10 writes 10 tenths in the tenths place.

items.q: Jayden’s pencil is 18.4 cm long. After sharpening, it is 2.6 cm shorter. How long is it now?
items.e: 18.4 − 2 = 16.4. Then take away 0.6: 16.4 − 0.4 = 16, and 16 − 0.2 = 15.8 cm. 16.2 does 6 − 4 in the tenths; 21 adds.

items.q: On a canoe trip, Sofia’s family paddles 3.6 km in the morning and 2.7 km in the afternoon. How much farther do they paddle in the morning?
items.e: Count up from 2.7: 0.3 makes 3, then 0.6 more makes 3.6. 0.3 + 0.6 = 0.9 km. 1.1 does 7 − 6 in the tenths; 6.3 is the total.

items.q: Zoe has a 1 L water bottle. She drinks 0.3 L at recess and 0.4 L at lunch. How much water is left?
items.e: She drinks 0.3 + 0.4 = 0.7 L. Then 1 − 0.7 = 0.3 L is left. 0.7 L is the amount she drinks.

items.q: Kai’s backpack has a mass of 3.4 kg. He takes out his 0.8 kg lunch bag and puts in a 1.5 kg library book. What is the mass of the backpack now?
items.e: Take away: 3.4 − 0.8 = 2.6. Then add: 2.6 + 1.5 = 4.1 kg. 2.6 kg stops after one step; 5.7 kg adds all three.
